neighbours.label: First piece of a split scientific-instrument or engineering word (mic|rometer, monoc|lonal, -c|ylinder, syn|chrotron): predicting the technical word's continuation
fire: The chemists measured the sample with a mass spectrometer overnight.
On the bench, an old oscilloscope showed the signal as a green wave.
Gravitational waves were detected by a giant laser interferometer.
The first cyclotron was built in Berkeley in the early 1930s.
Light passes through a collimator before it reaches the crystal.
Every microwave oven contains a magnetron that produces the waves.
Faint flashes are picked up by a photomultiplier tube under the tank.
The truck is powered by a quiet four-cylinder diesel engine.
quiet: The chemists measured the sample with a digital scale overnight.
On the bench, an old radio played music from a local station.
Gravitational waves were detected by a giant new detector.
The first library was built in Berkeley in the early 1930s.
Light passes through a window before it reaches the crystal.
Every kitchen contains a drawer that holds the spoons.
Faint flashes are picked up by a camera under the tank.
The truck is powered by a quiet electric engine.

predictions: Technical words split into pieces (spectrometer, oscilloscope, interferometer, cyclotron, collimator, magnetron, -cylinder) reach 0.3-0.8 on the first piece; the same sentence with a single-token word stays under 0.2.
short: first piece of a split technical word
notes: Probe: micrometeoroid 0.812, monoclonal 0.767, two-cylinder 0.620 (peak '-c'), micrometric 0.615, synchrotron 0.320; controls robotic 0.134, 'small label' 0.168, 'a rock' 0.163. Card logit effect promotes beam/ray/particle words. Splits checked with tok.py: spect|rometer, osc|illos|cope, interfer|ometer, cycl|otron, coll|imator, magnet|ron, phot|om|ulti|plier, four-c|ylinder.
